Skin.label: Skin
Skin.description: A thin, moist layer covering the whole body. Frogs can breathe through their skin, absorbing oxygen directly into the blood vessels just beneath it, which is why it must stay damp. It also absorbs water, so frogs rarely need to drink.

Heart.label: Heart
Heart.description: A three-chambered heart with two atria and one ventricle. The right atrium receives oxygen-poor blood from the body and the left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs and skin. Both empty into the single ventricle, which pumps blood out to the lungs, skin, and the rest of the body.
functions: Pumps blood through the whole body
Receives blood from the body, lungs and skin
Sends blood to the lungs and skin to pick up oxygen

Lungs.label: Lungs
Lungs.description: A pair of thin-walled, balloon-like sacs used for breathing on land. Frogs have no diaphragm, so they push air into the lungs by raising and lowering the floor of the mouth. The lungs share the work of gas exchange with the skin.
functions: Filled by pumping the floor of the mouth
Push air over the vocal cords for calling

Liver.label: Liver
Liver.description: The largest organ in the body cavity, made of several reddish-brown lobes. It produces bile to help digest fats, stores nutrients such as glycogen, and removes toxins from the blood.

Gallbladder.label: Gallbladder
Gallbladder.description: A small green sac tucked between the lobes of the liver. It stores bile made by the liver and releases it into the small intestine to help break down fats.
functions: Releases bile into the small intestine

Pancreas.label: Pancreas
Pancreas.description: A thin, pale organ lying along the curve of the stomach and small intestine. It releases digestive enzymes into the small intestine and produces hormones such as insulin that control blood sugar.
functions: Produces insulin to control blood sugar

Esophagus.label: Esophagus
Esophagus.description: A short muscular tube connecting the mouth to the stomach. Frogs swallow prey whole, and muscle contractions push food down the esophagus into the stomach.
functions: Carries food from the mouth to the stomach
Moves whole prey down with muscle contractions

Stomach.label: Stomach
Stomach.description: A curved, J-shaped organ on the left side of the body cavity. Its muscular walls churn food while acids and enzymes begin breaking down proteins, before passing the food on to the small intestine.
functions: Starts protein digestion with acids and enzymes
Passes food on to the small intestine

SmallIntestine.label: Small Intestine
SmallIntestine.description: A long, coiled tube where most digestion and nutrient absorption take place. Bile from the gallbladder and enzymes from the pancreas mix with food here, and nutrients pass through its walls into the blood.

LargeIntestine.label: Large Intestine
LargeIntestine.description: A short, wide tube at the end of the digestive tract. It absorbs water from undigested material and stores waste before it leaves the body through the cloaca.
functions: Stores waste until it leaves through the cloaca

Kidneys.label: Kidneys
Kidneys.description: A pair of long, dark red organs lying against the back wall of the body cavity. They filter waste from the blood and produce urine, and they help balance the water and salts in the frog's body.

Spleen.label: Spleen
Spleen.description: A small, round, dark red organ near the intestines. It is part of the immune and circulatory systems, filtering the blood, removing old red blood cells, and storing blood cells for later use.

Bladder.label: Bladder
Bladder.description: A thin-walled, two-lobed sac attached to the cloaca. It stores urine and can reabsorb water back into the body, helping the frog avoid drying out on land.
functions: Reabsorbs water to prevent drying out

tour.title: Welcome
tour.body: This short tour visits two key organs: the heart and the stomach. Use Next and Back to move between steps, or Skip to explore on your own.

tour.title: Heart
tour.body: The frog heart has three chambers: two atria and one ventricle. The ventricle pumps blood to the lungs and skin to pick up oxygen, and out to the rest of the body.

tour.title: Stomach
tour.body: Frogs swallow prey whole. Food slides down the esophagus into the J-shaped stomach, where strong muscles churn it and acids and enzymes start breaking it down.

tour.body: That's the tour! Click any organ to read about it and try Quiz me, or use the panel on the right to show and hide body systems.
